title: Squares of a Sorted Array
description:
Given an integer array `nums` sorted in **non-decreasing** order, return an array of the **squares of each number** sorted in non-decreasing order.

Try to solve the problem in `O(n)` time using two pointers rather than squaring and sorting.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Because the input array is sorted, the elements with the largest absolute values (and therefore the largest squares) are always at the two ends of the array.
Use two pointers, left at index 0 and right at index n - 1, and fill the result array from back to front.
At each step, place the larger of nums[left]^2 and nums[right]^2 at the current write position and move that pointer inward.

examples.explanation: After squaring, the array becomes [16, 1, 0, 9, 100]. After sorting in non-decreasing order, it becomes [0, 1, 9, 16, 100].
All values are negative, so their squares appear in strictly decreasing order and reverse to [1, 4, 9, 25].
